beats.text: Normal databases overwrite the old value.
beats.say: Most databases store only the current state. When a balance changes, the old value is overwritten, and the history is lost.

beats.text: Event sourcing: store every change as an event.
beats.say: Event sourcing flips that. Every change is stored as an immutable event, in an append-only log.
The current state is just the result of replaying those events from the beginning.

beats.text: Audit trail. Time travel. Replay to fix bugs.
beats.say: You get a full audit trail, you can rebuild the past at any point in time, and you can fix bugs by replaying events.

beats.text: Snapshots: replay only what came after.
beats.say: Replaying a million events would be slow, so systems take periodic snapshots, and replay only what came after.

beats.text: The cost: complexity and a separate read model.
beats.say: The cost: it's more complex, events can never change, and queries usually need a separate read model.
